parsed.refutation_attempt: I looked for any sanitization or validation of the url before it is concatenated into the command string. The code simply builds the command as executable + " \"" + url + "\"" (line 14) and then passes it to std::system (line 16). No checks on the content, length, or escaping of url are present. The proposed patch removes the surrounding quotes around url, which does not mitigate injection and actually introduces a syntax error on Windows (executable becomes "start \"" and the resulting command is "start \"http://…" without a closing quote). Therefore the vulnerability remains and the patch does not fix it.
